texto_para_tela: 590 REDBACK SPIDERS · 1955–1957 · AT LEAST 14 DEATHS BEFORE 1956 · NO CONFIRMED DEATH SINCE
credito_sugerido: Source: Wiener, Medical Journal of Australia, 2003; Winkel et al., Australian Family Physician, 2004
nota: Wiener: 'Between 1955 and 1957, I dissected the venom glands of 590 redback spiders for the production of antivenom' e 'No fatalities have occurred from redback spider bite since antivenom became available in 1956'. Winkel 2004: 'at least 14 deaths had been reported' e 'Since 1955, no deaths had been reported until a recent fatality following presumed redback spider bite in northern New South Wales that was not treated with [antivenom]'. E a Universidade de Melbourne (Pursuit, 17/01/2017): 'A man died from a red back spider bite in April 2016, the first spider bite death in more than 30 years'. O ABS não registra morte por aranha (X21) em 2016–2025. Por isso 'no CONFIRMED death since' na voz se sustenta, mas há duas mortes 'presumidas' em fontes lidas (antes de 2004 e em 2016): a tela nunca tira o 'CONFIRMED', e 'NO DEATH SINCE 1956' sozinho seria falso.

texto_aprovado: The redback, another of Australia's venomous spiders, is a less tidy story. Its antivenom was made by a scientist who dissected the venom glands of hundreds of spiders to do it. Redback bites killed at least 14 people before that antivenom arrived, in 1956, and there's been no confirmed death since.
